name: Opera House
bio: The sail-shelled performing arts centre on the harbour, one of the 20th century\'s great buildings.

name: Harbour Bridge
bio: The \"Coathanger\", a steel arch with a free pedestrian walkway, a BridgeClimb over the top and a pylon lookout.

name: Bondi Beach
bio: Australia\'s most famous beach, a golden crescent of surf, sand, and a scenic clifftop coastal walk.

name: Circular Quay
bio: The harbourfront ferry hub between the Opera House and the Rocks, where Sydney's ferries, cafés and promenade meet.

name: Royal Botanic Garden
bio: Harbourside botanic garden with walks around Farm Cove and views of the Opera House and Harbour Bridge.

name: The Rocks
bio: The historic precinct where Europeans first settled in 1788, with cobbled lanes, pubs and museums beneath the Harbour Bridge.

name: Darling Harbour
bio: A waterfront leisure precinct of museums, an aquarium, restaurants and a harbour promenade west of the city centre.

name: Taronga Zoo
bio: A hillside zoo on the north shore of the harbour, reached by a short ferry from Circular Quay.

name: Art Gallery of New South Wales
bio: The state art gallery in the Domain, with free general admission to its collection of Australian, Indigenous and European art.

name: Sydney Tower
bio: A 309 m observation tower in the city centre whose Sydney Tower Eye deck looks over the harbour and city.

name: Manly Beach
bio: An ocean surf beach reached by ferry from Circular Quay, backed by the pedestrian Corso and a sheltered harbour beach.

name: Watsons Bay
bio: A harbourside village at South Head with fish restaurants, a harbour beach and the cliffs of The Gap close by.

name: Mrs Macquarie's Chair
bio: A sandstone seat cut into the rock above Farm Cove, with classic views of the Opera House and Harbour Bridge.

name: Sydney Harbour National Park
bio: Harbour islands, headlands and foreshore walks, from Nielsen Park to North Head, protected as a national park inside the city.

name: Bondi to Coogee coastal walk
bio: A roughly 6 km clifftop walk linking Bondi, Tamarama, Bronte and Coogee beaches.

name: Cockatoo Island
bio: A UNESCO-listed convict and shipbuilding island in the harbour, with tours and camping, reached by ferry from Circular Quay.

name: Fort Denison
bio: The Pinchgut sandstone fort on a small island in the harbour, visited on a ferry tour from Circular Quay.

name: Luna Park Sydney
bio: A heritage amusement park on the north shore of the harbour, entered through a grinning giant face.

name: Queen Victoria Building
bio: An 1898 Romanesque arcade in the city centre, with a stained-glass dome and clock, now a shopping centre.

name: Hyde Park Barracks
bio: Convict-built barracks on Macquarie Street, now a museum of convict life with tours.

name: Australian National Maritime Museum
bio: A harbourside maritime museum at Darling Harbour with the destroyer HMAS Vampire and a replica of HMB Endeavour.

name: Sea Life Sydney Aquarium
bio: A ticketed aquarium at Darling Harbour with penguins, platypus and sharks.

name: Australian Museum
bio: Australia's first museum, with natural history and Indigenous cultures galleries beside Hyde Park.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
bio: A contemporary art museum in a 1930s art-deco building on Circular Quay.

name: Sydney Fish Market
bio: A working fish market at Pyrmont open every day, with seafood stalls and restaurants in a new 2026 building.

name: Coogee Beach
bio: A surf beach at the southern end of the Bondi to Coogee walk, with ocean pools and cafés.

name: Bronte Beach
bio: A surf beach with ocean baths and a grassy park, on the Bondi to Coogee walk.

name: Bondi Icebergs
bio: A clifftop ocean pool and club at the south end of Bondi Beach, with a restaurant overlooking the water.

name: Tamarama Beach
bio: A small surf beach in a cove between Bondi and Bronte.

name: Centennial Park
bio: A 189 ha historic parkland with ponds, cycling and horse-riding tracks.

name: North Head
bio: A headland at the harbour entrance with clifftop walks, lookouts over the Pacific and whale watching.

name: Quarantine Station
bio: A former quarantine station on North Head, visited on day and night heritage tours.

name: Chinatown
bio: The Dixon Street district of Asian restaurants and shops in Haymarket.

name: Anzac Memorial
bio: An art-deco war memorial in Hyde Park with a Hall of Memory and a museum exhibition, open daily.

name: Sydney Observatory
bio: Australia's oldest observatory, on Observatory Hill, with telescopes and a planetarium.

name: Walsh Bay
bio: A precinct of heritage harbour wharves with a theatre and restaurants, walkable to Barangaroo.

name: Chinese Garden of Friendship
bio: A Ming-style Chinese garden at Darling Harbour.

name: White Rabbit Gallery
bio: A private gallery of contemporary Chinese art in Chippendale.

name: Wendy Whiteley's Secret Garden
bio: A hidden garden grown on a former rail yard at Lavender Bay, with harbour views.

name: Vaucluse House
bio: An 1803 harbourside mansion with gardens, now a house museum.

name: Nielsen Park
bio: A harbourside park with a sheltered beach and picnic grounds in Sydney Harbour National Park.

name: The Gap
bio: A cliff lookout at South Head above the Pacific.

name: South Head
bio: A heritage headland at the harbour entrance, with Hornby Lighthouse and the South Head Heritage Trail.

name: Bradleys Head
bio: A harbour promontory reached from Taronga Zoo wharf, with walks and city views.

name: Middle Head
bio: A bushland headland walk past coastal artillery fortifications.

name: Chowder Bay
bio: A harbour bay with a beach, cafés and former naval installations, on the Bradleys Head to Chowder Bay walk.

name: Balmoral Beach
bio: A sheltered family beach with a swimming enclosure and a bathers' pavilion.

name: Shelly Beach
bio: A sheltered beach near Manly used for diving and snorkelling.

name: Clovelly Beach
bio: A sheltered, wave-free swimming beach in a long inlet.

name: Maroubra Beach
bio: A broad surf beach in the southern eastern suburbs.

name: Malabar Headland National Park
bio: Coastal walks and cliff views on a headland between Maroubra and Malabar.

name: Kamay Botany Bay National Park
bio: The headlands of Kurnell and La Perouse at Botany Bay, site of Captain Cook's 1770 landing.

name: La Perouse
bio: A headland village at Kamay Botany Bay with a museum and access to Bare Island.

name: Bare Island
bio: An 1880s fort on an island reached by footbridge at La Perouse, with guided tours.

name: Cape Solander
bio: A Kurnell headland lookout known for whale watching and its cliff walk.

name: Cronulla Beach
bio: A string of surf beaches with an esplanade and surf schools, reached by train from the city.

name: Narrabeen Beach
bio: A long surf beach that hosts professional surf events.

name: Collaroy Beach
bio: A calm beach good for learning to surf.

name: Dee Why Beach
bio: A busy surf beach with cafés beside Dee Why Lagoon.

name: Curl Curl Beach
bio: A popular beach with a cliff playground and café.

name: Freshwater Beach
bio: A surf beach at Harbord.

name: Long Reef Beach
bio: A headland beach beside the Long Reef Aquatic Reserve.

name: Great North Walk
bio: A 250 km multi-day trail from Sydney to Newcastle, walked in day sections.

name: Lane Cove National Park
bio: Bushland along the Lane Cove River with walks and canoeing.

name: Garigal National Park
bio: Sandstone bushland with waterfalls and Middle Harbour views on the north side of the city.

name: Berowra Valley National Park
bio: Valley bushland along Berowra Creek, crossed by the Great North Walk.

name: Sydney Olympic Park
bio: The 2000 Olympics site, now parkland with sports venues and walks.

name: Brickpit Ring Walk
bio: An elevated walkway around the former State Brickworks pit in Sydney Olympic Park.

name: Old Government House
bio: A UNESCO World Heritage colonial governors' residence in Parramatta Park.

name: Elizabeth Farm
bio: A homestead begun in 1793, the oldest surviving European building in Australia.

name: The Bay Run
bio: A 7 km car-free circuit track around Iron Cove.

name: Koala Park Sanctuary
bio: A koala sanctuary at Dural with kangaroo feeding.

name: Featherdale Wildlife Park
bio: A wildlife park at Doonside with koalas and kangaroo feeding.

name: Australian Botanic Garden Mount Annan
bio: A native-plant botanic garden with a visitor centre, south-west of the city.

name: NSW Rail Museum
bio: A heritage steam train and rail museum at Thirlmere.

name: Heathcote National Park
bio: Heath and waterholes near Waterfall with bushwalks and mountain biking.

name: Dharawal National Park
bio: Waterfalls, rock pools and bushland near Helensburgh.
